reason: Conversation 1 is concise, accepts that the customer won't open the machine, and quickly escalates to Candy support or the warranty provider without encouraging internal work. It does overstate the cause somewhat ('likely' an internal fuse or board) and repeats the generic safety panel, but it stays fairly uncertain. Conversation 2 is long and repeatedly suggests internal checks the customer has refused (multimeter test of the thermal cut-out, swapping it, a rear reset button), makes claims about capacitor dangers and about the board that are speculative, and wastes turns on checks already done. It does have the better warranty advice, but that does not outweigh its pushing of internal DIY and its poorer efficiency.
